quest.title: A Swordmaster's Path Is Paved With Broken Blades
quest.description: The swordmaster who aimed to be the greatest under heaven descended into madness after losing his Vision. You decide to help his disciples investigate the cause...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x800, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia

talks.objective: Find the next person who lost their Vision

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The third person who had their Vision taken is supposed to be a famous swordmaster around these parts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon heard that he's the present-day master of Meikyou Shisui Art... sounds pretty impressive...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is his dojo, luckily there's some people around. Let's go talk to them.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Nanako, don't worry! Sensei will be fine...

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Those thugs that challenged the dojo were strong, but he fought them all off in the end, didn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Maybe, but I'm still worried about him...

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Things have gotten dangerous before in the past, but it's never shaken him. This time, though... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: It's just because he's been possessed, that's all! Once the exorcism has taken place, he'll be right as rain in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there... did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: ...Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: I don't care whether you're trespassers or just here to harass us while Sensei is impaired — get out of here immediately!

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Don't make me draw my blade, or you won't live to regret it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—No, you got us all wrong! We just came here to... uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're here to become disciples.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: ...Disciples?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup yup! We've heard all about the mighty master of Meikyou Shisui Art. It's the whole reason we came all this way — to seek him out and ask him to train us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But then we got here and overheard you talking about how he got possessed, or something...

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Hmm... From the way you're dressed... it doesn't look like you're from around here.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Please accept my apologies... We've had so many people trying to cause us trouble recently that we're on high alert.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: You haven't arrived at the best of times, I'm afraid. Sensei got possessed recently, and he's still recovering. He's not able to take on any new disciples for the time being.

choices.text: We can wait till he's recovered.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: I see you are earnest in your pursuit. *sigh* Okay, how about this — my fellow disciple Nanako and I will explain Sensei's situation to you in a little more detail. Then you can decide whether to stay or to leave.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: Sensei's name is Domon, a name I'm sure you've already heard.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: Though self-taught, he mastered the art of the sword to a high level. He then proceeded to defeat many other prominent swordmasters, never losing a single fight.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: He once said that his goal was to become the best swordmaster in the world.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: And so, even while training us, he continued to hone his own art. His fervor truly inspired us, and we trained hard, determined to keep up with him.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: But then...

response.speaker: Nanako
response.text: Not long ago, Sensei had his Vision taken away. He hasn't been the same since.

response.speaker: Nanako
response.text: He says the strangest things over and over, and he refuses to let us train...

response.speaker: Nanako
response.text: Junya and I have discussed it, and we both think that he's been possessed by an evil spirit. So, we've asked the shrine maidens from the Grand Narukami Shrine to perform an exorcism.

response.speaker: Nanako
response.text: But if I'm honest... I still have my doubts over whether he'll completely recover...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Grand Narukami Shrine? What's that?

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: You haven't heard of it? It's the largest shrine on Narukami Island. The head shrine maiden is reputed to have very close ties with the Almighty Shogun herself.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: Not that we'd have any means of involving the head shrine maiden, of course... But even one of the ordinary shrine maidens from the Grand Narukami Shrine would have clear power and authority to perform an exorcism.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: So don't worry, Nanako. Sensei is going to be just fine.

response.speaker: Junya
response.text: The exorcism will take place this evening. You're both more than welcome to come and watch if you're interested.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... losing your Vision can cause possession? Uh, guess we should come back this evening and see for ourselves.

choices.text: I'm not going back until I can call him my sensei.

talks.objective: Wait until night for the exorcism (18:00 – 24:00)

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Shh... So, you decided to come? It's a good thing you didn't arrive any earlier — you would have had to witness Sensei in one of his fits of madness.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Just now, when Nanako was attending to him, she heard him whispering a few names to himself.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: When she asked him who the people were, he suddenly looked panic-stricken and pushed her away.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: It looked like he was in great distress... He was covering his ears and looking frantically around him with bloodshot eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: All the while he kept calling those names — some of them we knew, others we didn't recognize, but they all seemed to be the names of swordmasters he had defeated in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: One of them was Anzai. He used to be a fellow disciple of Sensei's, his senior, in fact. But Sensei defeated him in a duel many years ago, and he has been a wanderer ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Sensei wouldn't stop calling his name... *sigh* Thankfully, the shrine maidens managed to subdue him, so the exorcism can finally continue.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: The ritual has now begun — all we can do is patiently await the result. Here's hoping Sensei will be back to his normal self very soon.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Please excuse me for a moment while I fetch some water. If he wakes up, he is sure to be thirsty.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's that sneaking around? Uh-oh... could they be here to mess up the exorcism?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We won't let them get away with it! Come on, let's go after them!

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: *sigh* I just hope Sensei doesn't have to endure this much longer...
How... How did you... catch up with me... so quickly...
Are you sure you're Domon's disciples? You move even quicker than he does...
Unless... I guess it's been a few years. Maybe his skills have improved again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, excuse me! We're the ones asking the questions here! First off, who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what are you doing, sneaking around these parts, hmm? You seem like bad news, mister!
Bad news? Hmph. I'll have you know I trained side-by-side with Domon back in the day — long before you ever showed up.
I don't care to talk about that time anymore... but if you must know, I am Domon's senior.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: His senior? Wait, that means you must be...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Anzai. Yes, that's me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did you run?

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Because I don't wish to see Domon, or anyone else associated with him, ever again.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: When we were young, we trained under the same swordmaster, studying Meikyou Shisui Art together.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: I had begun training five years before him, and everyone looked up to me as a steady and dependable older disciple.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Practitioners of Meikyou Shisui Art seek to achieve "stillness of mind, freedom from all agitation." So the majority of disciples are indifferent to rank and reward. I was no exception.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: But Domon was different. The first thing he did when he joined was go straight to our sensei and ask him, with a beaming smile on his face, how to become the best in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Sensei scolded him, and told him that the art of the sword should not be used for such vain ends. Sensei said that coveting the title of the best swordmaster, barely days into his training, showed that he had a fickle mind, and that this would impede him from ever mastering the blade.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: I thought so too, at the time... But Domon began making swift progress in his training, and even started catching up with me.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Only then did I realize that it was Domon who had long since freed his mind from all agitation.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: He was consumed by his singular desire to become the best in the world. He sought nothing less than perfection in the art of the sword, and nothing could deter him from this goal, no matter what stood in his way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure sounds like he meant business... So, how come you don't want to ever see him again?

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Because until he arrived, I was convinced that I would succeed our sensei as the master of Meikyou Shisui Art.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Of all the disciples, I was the most gifted — I had trained the longest. Everyone had high expectations for me.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Domon's arrival changed everything. When we sparred, I lost not just the match, but my pride and my status, too. I fled the dojo that day and never looked back.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Later, I heard that he sparred with Sensei, too. Sensei was advanced in years by then, and unfortunately, that match used up every last ounce of energy in his body...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: After that, I wanted nothing further to do with him. Deep down, though, I still respected his mastery of the blade, and his commitment to the art of the sword.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: So when I heard rumors that he had lost his mind, my first reaction was to dismiss them as false. How could he, of all people, have lost his mind? His mind was the sharpest of them all — he had practiced Meikyou Shisui Art to perfection.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: I decided to quietly come and see if it were true. Then, to my complete astonishment, I heard him call my name... I thought mine was a name he had long since forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: So you see — I came here not to cause him any harm. I just wanted to see for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: ...Okay, you've heard my story. You should get back now — the exorcism is probably finishing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Seems like we got it wrong this time. He wasn't here to mess up the exorcism at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Paimon's not sure we should bring him back with us... Uh, let's go see how the exorcism's coming along!

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: What? You're saying he isn't possessed?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Does that mean he's just lost his mind? But how is that possible? ...No, I refuse to believe it. Something's clearly wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Nanako, please, try not to get agitated...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I am sorry. With what powers I have, I can find no sign of any malignant spirit having possessed Domon.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: But spirits may take a myriad of forms in this world, many of which I cannot claim to have witnessed myself. Thus, I dare not rule out possession with complete certainty.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: And all is certainly not lost, for I received word not long ago that Lady Yae has taken an interest in your sensei's case.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: L—Lady Yae? Is that... the same Lady Yae that I think you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: The head shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine? That's wonderful news! Then Sensei will be sure to recover...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Correct. Lady Yae is most knowledgeable indeed, and has abundant experience in the exorcism of evil spirits and aversion of great calamities.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I am unable to say for certain whether an evil spirit has possessed your sensei, but Lady Yae can give a conclusive verdict.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Miss Inagi, but I must ask. Should we prepare a greeting gift for Lady Yae?

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary. All that is required of you is your timely arrival at the Grand Narukami Shrine. Lady Yae does not like to be kept waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: I must leave now, but we will meet soon at the shrine. I wish Domon a full and speedy recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Who'd have thought Lady Yae herself would have taken notice of our sensei's case...

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Do you mean to say that Sensei isn't renowned enough to deserve Lady Yae's attention?

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: No, no, that's not what I meant at all! You misunderstand me.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: I just mean... this is Lady Yae, the head shrine maiden! She has direct and close contact with the Almighty Shogun herself!

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Ahem. Anyway, you should join us too, tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Given that you've traveled all this way just to meet our sensei, we the disciples of Meikyou Shisui Art will do our best to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will gladly join you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! After all, everyone seems pretty excited about Lady Yae. We're curious to meet her, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who knows, maybe we'll be able to find out a thing or two about the Raiden Shogun from her...

talks.objective: Go to Grand Narukami Shrine to see the head shrine maiden

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—D'you think that's Lady Yae...? No wonder Junya was so excited... she has a really striking presence...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, is it just Paimon, or did she look right at us just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Eh, it was probably nothing... It's not like she's ever seen us before.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: Keep away... Keep away from me...

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I gave up the art of the sword... Please, let me go, I beg you...

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: As you can see, Lady Yae.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Domon has persisted in this state for some time now. He appears to see those who have lost to him in duels past, gathered all around him to persecute him.

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Lady Yae, it must be a possession... right?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: This is nothing like him at all. In the past, no matter what came his way, he would always face it with a confident smile.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I am sorry. It is clear to me that your sensei is not possessed by any evil spirit.

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: But... Then, d—does that mean he...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm, yes. This is a change in the person himself.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Unable to cope with the tremendous pressure he was under, he suffered a spiritual collapse. With his wits impaired, he finally descended into madness.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As one who is thrown into the sea, though he fights back desperately against his predicament, it does nothing to prevent his descent into the depths.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: As for what has triggered this change, I believe it must be the loss of his Vision. For to be stripped of one's Vision is to be stripped of one's ambition.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Stripped of his ambition...? But, Lady Yae, even without his ambition, why should he suffer such a dramatic change? How does that explain his descent into madness?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Your school practices Meikyou Shisui Art, does it not?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: "Stillness of mind, freedom from all agitation"... What a fine notion that would be, if any in this world could ever hope to achieve it...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: There was once one who claimed to be indifferent to rank and reward, and who fled enraged when defeated by his junior. And then there was an aged swordmaster who was aggrieved enough that he crossed blades with a disciple he himself had taught.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Then, what of the one who crossed blades with his own sensei and beloved fellow disciple, and defeated them both? Can one truly remain unagitated, of still mind, in moments such as these?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Lady Yae... I'm not sure I understand...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The path of the swordmaster is filled with twists and turns. It is no small undertaking to pursue the position of greatest swordmaster in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It requires one to take their sword firmly in both hands and cut down the hopes and dreams of others... even those of one's closest companions.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Only a deep commitment to his ambition to become the best made it possible for him to rise above the pain of these encounters — to focus on the way ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: When that ambition disappeared, he began to doubt himself. As he battled his growing anxiety... he slowly descended into the state you see him in now.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Heh... Much like a certain fatally flawed friend of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Poor Sensei... To think he's been suffering so greatly...

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... It's all my fault...

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: Father, Sensei... Anzai...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: That's enough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't that Anzai? Where'd he come from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did he follow us the whole way here?

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: Anzai... Why are there two of you...? Is that you, or a ghost?

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: You're here for revenge, aren't you... I knew it would come... I never should have—

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: You're right to assume that my feelings towards you are far from kindly. *sigh* But I didn't come here to settle a score.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: It's been so long now that I made peace with it years ago. You did nothing wrong that day, I just... I couldn't face the humiliation. That's why I ran.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: I don't think most of the people you beat along the way would hold it against you. On the contrary, when you cut our ambitions short, we entrusted them to you, in the hope that they might carry you further.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Now, I know that we can't place our hopes in you any longer, since you've been stripped of your ambitions, too...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: But that is no reason to strip them of theirs! "Follow the way of the sword all the way to the highest peak." You taught them that, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: But, what if one day... the same thing happens to them...

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I put everything I had into trying to become the best... but what if it was all a huge mistake, right from the start?

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: If there's a chance they'll end up like me one day, I'd rather they stay where they are now than go any further down this path...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: ...Have you asked them what they think?

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: Sensei... After you rescued me from the hands of the pirates, I told myself I would follow in your footsteps for the rest of my days.

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: I can't know whether I will suffer in my future as you do now. All I know is that here and now, in the present, I wish to continue.

dialogues.speaker: Nanako
dialogues.text: I want to keep going until the day that I can stand before everyone with my head held high and announce that I, like my sensei Domon before me, am a master of Meikyou Shisui Art!

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Nanako's far from the only one... Actually, all of us think that way.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: Goodness... Well, I...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: You see? You can place the ambition you once had in their hands.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Being stripped of your ambition is something that's never happened to me, so I can't claim to understand it. But I do know what it feels like to have your ambitions crushed... that's what happened on the day that you so effortlessly defeated me.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: So, just as I once placed my ambitions onto you, it is time for you to release yours into their custody.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: You are not in the same position that I was. When I left, I had nothing to my name, but you have a great number of worthy disciples.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I... I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I am sorry to have made you worry for me and for the state of Meikyou Shisui Art.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: I no longer have the resolve to become the best in the world... the emptiness and suffering inside of me will not abate, so I cannot hope to still my mind and be free of agitation.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: But as your sensei, I shall commit to imparting unto you everything I have learned in my life so far.

dialogues.speaker: Domon
dialogues.text: This is my promise, and I humbly ask Anzai, my senior, to hold me to my word.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: You can count on that. I'd be checking in on you occasionally anyway, just to make sure you hadn't lost your mind again...

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: But I am now used to the life of a wanderer. I do not belong in the dojo anymore. So I will simply stop by once in a while to make sure you aren't cutting any corners with them.

dialogues.speaker: Anzai
dialogues.text: Well, don't just stand there staring at me. Say thank you to Lady Yae and then get yourself back home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, even though his ambition was taken away, his disciples can take it over on his behalf. Guess that sorta solves this one, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, it seems as good of a resolution as we can hope for.

dialogues.speaker: Inagi Hotomi
dialogues.text: Traveler, a moment, please. Lady Yae has some words for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...So, my intuition was correct.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The wind that blows from afar carries fresh life to these shores...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: For us to meet now is premature. Nevertheless, you set foot on these islands at precisely the right moment.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm... I have high hopes for you, child. Don't disappoint me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Lady Yae seems to have taken a real interest in you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She seems super mysterious... Paimon's so curious what she really meant by all of that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, we can come back to it another time. For now, we should go report back to Miss Kamisato.

dialogues.speaker: Junya
dialogues.text: Sensei will be fine, I'm sure of it. He's a strong person.

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: *sigh* Only after following Captain Beidou across the lands did I realize that Liyue was best...

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: Well, I say that, but I've never really gotten off the boat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, as for that next leg of the journey...

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: Nope, sorry, that's confidential. I can only tell you that we're going to Sumeru next.

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: I can't say much more, and I'd suggest that you refrain from asking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: Alright. Hope things go well with you!

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: At this point, we've got enough to determine the general area in which these Ruin machines are located. But we still can't pinpoint their precise location.

choices.text: How's the view from the shore?

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: You mean from here? Well, it's certainly wider than it was below deck. It's not bad.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Still, I'm not very fond of the air here. It's just missing that little "something" that I usually have below deck. I swear it's making my brain work slower.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: The shore's good for a view, but not great for thinking.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Which is why I'm just wringing my hands over here. Guess the rest is up to you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gee, this lady couldn't beg and plead to save her life!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Hehe~

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Not great. Well, I'm stuck, to be honest.

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: Phew, we're almost there. Once this is over, I'll be able to return to the ship!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Quite alright, quite alright. I've remained onshore enough, and I've made great progress in my research. Our sampling order is just about complete!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Hahah! To think that we were able to get this done without the Captain's help... I can't wait to see how shocked she'll be at our progress!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your progress in making me do your job for you, you mean?

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Oh, and, ah... your progress, of course! It's been quite splendid, it has!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Guess Captain Beidou's got some unreliable subordinates too, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: *yawn* So sleepy... What's so good about being on land, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: Ah, hello there Traveler! Thanks for your help thus far.

dialogues.speaker: Muzhen
dialogues.text: It's all thanks to you that we've got enough for the Captain to complete the order.

choices.text: Who would want this stuff, anyway...

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Aye, rather dangerous-looking, eh?

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Well, our next objective is Sumeru, and I suppose only those weird researchers would study these things, anyway.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: They aren't like those traveling scholars who wander about outdoors. I believe they're people more akin to myself — technical experts who spend most of their time in their studies researching items.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: I would guess that those ruins don't just contain these few machines, either...

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: If you're interested, you can continue to explore those ruins and pass any components you find to me. I'll pay well for them!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: After all, "the more the merrier" is the watchword here, both for us and for our client in Sumeru!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: Yes. My share of the work's basically done. I'm only needed again once the cargo inspection has been completed.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: As a result, Sea Drake kicked me back onto the shore.

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: "Stop cooping yourself up in your cabin. Get some of that sea breeze, it'll do you some good." Hmph, he should just speak for himself!

response.speaker: Muzhen
response.text: *yawn* Well, if there's nothing else, I'll be taking a nap now. Please excuse me...
